label: live

steps.assertion: The Pro project terminal opens in its registered dedicated checkout.
The dev-madrid device terminal uses the existing relay and prints the actual remote hostname.
Type or dictate a command and Run send echo hello through the real PTY.
Sticky Ctrl and C interrupt sleep within two seconds and preserve its non-zero exit record.
Reload reconnects the same terminal and replays hello in its scrollback.
The copy buttons include exactly the requested command range and strip every escape code.

steps.assertion: Send to… delivers the last command to the coordinator and starts its next turn.

evidence.text:
The owner sent output from the terminal on Goncalos-MacBook-Pro.local in /Users/ggomes/jevellan-projects/jevellan-live-sandbox:

record-6

steps.assertion: Take over in browser attaches a real native thread session; leaving detaches and returns it to Jevellan.
Every captured screen passes the dedicated live vision rubric in this layout.

screens.expected: a connected project terminal with usable controls and no clipped text

cosmetic: The header path is cut off with an ellipsis ('/Users/ggome...'), so the full project path can't be read.
The key row is clipped on the right: a partly visible key sits past the → key. It looks like a scrollable row, but nothing shows that it scrolls.
Terminal output breaks words across lines ('jevellan-l' / 'ive-sandbox'), which makes the path harder to read.
The 'Type straight into terminal' checkbox label is small and low-contrast.

screens.expected: a connected dev-madrid terminal with the remote hostname and usable controls

cosmetic: The Terminal header sits tight against the 'Conversations' bar, and the top edge of its menu button looks slightly clipped
There are two menu buttons, one in the Conversations bar and one in the Terminal header, which is redundant
The last key in the shortcut row is cut off at the right edge; it is probably reachable by scrolling, but nothing shows the row scrolls
The output repeats 'hostname' before the prompt line, so the typed command is shown twice

screens.expected: terminal copy and Send to controls reachable at this layout

cosmetic: The shortcut key row is cut off at both edges: the first key ('→') is clipped on the left and the '…' key is clipped on the right. It looks like a horizontally scrolling row, but nothing on screen shows that it scrolls.
The host and path text in the header ('Goncalos-MacBook-Pro.local · /Users/ggome...') is cut off at the right edge.
The shell prompt is long ('ggomes@Goncalos-MacBook-Pro jevellan-live-sandbox %'), so it wraps onto two lines and makes the terminal output harder to scan.
The 'Copied' confirmation is plain, unstyled text sitting between the buttons and the command input, so it is easy to miss.

screens.expected: a browser terminal attached to a native coding session with usable exit controls

cosmetic: The header subtitle 'dev-madrid scenarios · /home/gg…' is cut off with an ellipsis, so the full workspace path isn't shown in the header.
The terminal wraps lines in the middle of words ('C laude', 'Jeve llan', 'scena rios', 'threa d_'), which makes them harder to read.
The start of the attach command is scrolled out of view at the top of the terminal (it begins mid-line at "/bin/jevellan.mjs' thread attach").
The last button in the special-key row is cut off at the right edge. The row seems to scroll sideways, but nothing shows that more keys are there.
The sticky 'Take over thread' header sits tight against the 'Conversations' bar above it, with the top bar partly covered.

The native Claude Code session is stopped at the workspace trust prompt and hasn't started yet. The exit controls still work: 'No, exit' in the prompt, the Esc key and the 'Close terminal' button are all visible and reachable.

observations: Usage records come from runtime-reported turn outcomes. Missing tokens or cost remain unknown; minutes include concurrent sessions.
